content:
Isabella Rossi: seeing a correctness failure in the INT8 matmul path when running the harness on A100. It doesn’t crash, but outputs diverge hard vs BF16 baseline (max abs diff ~3.2, relative diff spikes). This is on the `int8_w8a8` mode from the latest branch.

Isabella Rossi: repro case (from the matrix runner, pulled one failing artifact):
- GPU: A100-SXM4-80GB
- model: `hosted-llama-3-8b` (prefill microbench)
- op: MLP proj matmul (one of the GEMMs)
- shape: M=1, K=14336, N=4096
- batch=12, concurrent=24 (end-to-end), but I can repro in microbench with M=1
- kernel selected: `cutlass_i8i8_s8_accum` (from registry)

Isabella Rossi: log snippet:
```
[matmul] mode=int8_w8a8 selected_kernel=cutlass_i8i8_s8_accum m=1 n=4096 k=14336
[matmul] scales: act=per_token, w=per_channel
[check] compare_to=bf16 max_abs=3.19 p99_abs=0.88 mean_abs=0.14
[check] FAIL threshold_abs=0.02 threshold_p99=0.01
```

Grace Kim: :eyes: thanks. does it fail deterministically run-to-run?

Isabella Rossi: yep. same seed, same prompt. fails every time. if I force fallback to bf16 via flag it passes.

Yuki Sato: do we know if the selected kernel supports M=1? some of the i8 paths are only validated for M>=16 / M multiple-of-something.

Rina Kobayashi: +1. also we might be mixing “int8 kernel supports shape” vs “int8 quant config supports this layer” (scale layout / alignment).

Grace Kim: can you try M=16 with same K/N? want to see if it’s a small-M epilogue issue.

Isabella Rossi: tried:
- M=16, K=14336, N=4096 -> passes (max_abs ~0.006)
- M=8 -> passes borderline (max_abs ~0.03) depending on threshold
- M=1 -> always fails badly

Hiro Tanaka: that looks like a kernel correctness issue for tiny M. we should guard and fallback until we have a verified small-M implementation.

Noah Patel: we already intended to have shape guardrails for INT8 dispatch (esp for decode / M small). if a guard is missing, fix is: refuse this kernel for M < min_m (likely 8 or 16), and route to baseline.

Yuki Sato: in decode, M is often tokens being processed (can be 1), so this is a big one.

Rina Kobayashi: what’s our current guard logic? is it only checking K alignment / stride? maybe we didn’t include an M check.

Grace Kim: pulling the relevant bit from the branch (from memory):
- checks: (K % 16 == 0), (N % 8 == 0), (contiguous), and (gpu_capability in {sm80, sm90})
- I don’t recall a min_M.

Julian Moore: this might be why E2E looks ok in prefill-heavy cases but decode sanity fails when you isolate it.

Isabella Rossi: also tried forcing `cublaslt_i8` (we have it behind env var): M=1 passes. perf is worse, but it’s correct.

Hiro Tanaka: good datapoint. suggests our cutlass path has a corner case, not quantization itself.

Grace Kim: action: add guard for cutlass int8 matmul kernel: `if (M < 16) fallback`. maybe also `M % 8 == 0`? but simplest is hard min.

Noah Patel: agree. better to be conservative in the first rollout. we can open a follow-up to investigate / add a correct small-M kernel.

Rina Kobayashi: pls also log why we fall back (one-line reason). makes canary debugging easier.

Sahana Iyer: if we add a guard, I can add a CI smoke test that includes an M=1 case and asserts it chooses fallback and stays within numeric threshold.

Yuki Sato: question: should the fallback be BF16 or FP16? baseline for this model is BF16.

Grace Kim: fallback should be baseline dtype for the run (bf16). don’t silently change precision.

Isabella Rossi: +1. right now fallback is “default matmul implementation” which is bf16 in this config.

Hiro Tanaka: any other constraints we should add while here? e.g., some of these kernels require `K % 32 == 0` for certain layouts.

Noah Patel: careful: K=14336 is divisible by 32 (448*32), so this case wouldn’t be caught by that. it really seems M-related.

Grace Kim: ok. I’ll put up a patch in the dispatch:
- `if (m < 16) return false;` for `cutlass_i8i8_s8_accum`
- also add telemetry: `matmul_fallback_reason="int8_cutlass_min_m"`

Rina Kobayashi: can you also add a unit test for the selector? we’ve had regressions where registry changed and guard didn’t apply.

Grace Kim: yep. will add a selector test in `runtime/tests/dispatch/test_int8_guards.cc` (or similar) with the exact failing shape.

Isabella Rossi: I’ll re-run the failing artifact after your patch lands.

Julian Moore: FYI: scheduler mixed workload uses M=1 a lot in decode slices. this fallback is acceptable; perf impact is limited to decode matmuls on int8 path.

Yuki Sato: do we want to gate INT8 entirely for decode? or just this kernel.

Hiro Tanaka: not gate entirely. cublaslt path is correct for M=1; also we may have other correct kernels. just block the broken one.

Noah Patel: +1. we should also update the registry entry to include `min_m: 16` so it’s data-driven.

Grace Kim: good idea. we can add min_m to the kernel registry schema, but that might be bigger. for sprint, code guard is fine; registry enhancement as follow-up.

Sahana Iyer: for CI smoke: I’ll assert that when m=1, selected_kernel != cutlass_i8i8_s8_accum and error metrics pass. when m=16, it’s allowed.

Isabella Rossi: :thumbsup: adding extra numbers: on H100, the same case does *not* fail (M=1 passes). so it’s sm80-specific.

Grace Kim: helpful. guard should probably be conditional `sm80 && m<16` (or be conservative across all). since H100 passes, but we don’t want to assume it’s always safe.

Hiro Tanaka: start with `m < 16` across all arch for this kernel. less risk. we can loosen later after more coverage.

Yuki Sato: ok but that means we’ll never use this cutlass int8 kernel for decode anywhere, which is acceptable for now.

Noah Patel: decode is latency-sensitive but also where correctness matters most. fallback is fine.

Rina Kobayashi: please add a note to the sprint daily: “INT8 cutlass matmul guarded for M<16 due to sm80 correctness bug; fallback enabled”.

Grace Kim: will do. pushing patch in ~30m.

Isabella Rossi: thanks all. I’ll watch for the PR link.

Grace Kim: PR up: `pr-19841` follow-up commit (same PR): “Guard cutlass INT8 matmul for small-M; add fallback reason metric; add selector unit test”.

Sahana Iyer: I’ll add the CI case in `pr-19926` once this merges, or I can stack it if you want.

Grace Kim: stack is fine if you can rebase quickly.

Isabella Rossi: pulled the branch w/ guard, reran failing microbench:
- M=1 now selects fallback (bf16) and passes thresholds
- M=16 still selects cutlass int8 and passes

Isabella Rossi: end-to-end harness also clean now. :white_check_mark:

Hiro Tanaka: nice. let’s make sure release notes call out the guard (so no one expects int8 decode matmuls to be accelerated yet).

Rina Kobayashi: and add to regression triage playbook: “if int8 enabled and decode looks slower than expected, check min_m guard + fallback reason metric”.

Grace Kim: ack. merging after CI green.
